title: Private VPC runtime graceful switchover with health-first rollout
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement an automated, health-first rolling upgrade strategy for Private (VPC) data-plane runtime nodes that guarantees zero-or-minimal downtime for tenant traffic. The goal is to provide: 1) an infra-driven rollout operator (Terraform + operator hooks) that can coordinate node replacement in VPC/private installs; 2) standardized health checks and pre-upgrade validation (priming, KV cache warmup, smoke generation); 3) an automated rollback trigger when health signals degrade beyond configured thresholds. This ticket covers IaC module changes, controller orchestration behavior, and runbook updates for on-prem customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Upgrades initiated via the Terraform module apply path or the upgrade operator follow a health-first sequence: pre-checks -> create new node -> validate -> shift traffic -> drain old node -> finalize. 2) No more than 2 minutes of tail latency increase for 99th percentile on affected tenants during a normal upgrade in staging, and rollouts auto-abort and rollback within configured window when error-rate > 3x baseline or 99p latency regresses > 50%. 3) All rollout steps are observable in the Console with per-tenant timeline and per-node health metrics. 4) IaC changes are backward compatible for existing installs; new variables are optional with sane defaults. 5) Documentation and runbook updated with manual override instructions and postmortem checklist.
implementation_notes: Architecture: Upgrade operator runs in the customer control plane (or operator for on-prem). Terraform module exposes an 'upgrade_plan' resource that triggers the operator via a webhook or CRD. Operator behavior: 1) Run pre-upgrade gating (disk, version compatibility, config drift checks). 2) Provision replacement node(s) with the target runtime image using the same instance profile and security group. 3) Perform priming traffic to warm KV cache and JIT kernels. 4) Run integration smoke tests (generation at low-RPS, embedding tests) mirrored against a traffic-shim. 5) Mark new node Ready only after health gates pass. 6) Shift traffic using NLB weight adjustments and session affinity handling. 7) Drain old node gracefully respecting in-flight KV caches and token streams. 8) If health gates fail at any stage, run automatic rollback which reprovisions previous version and reattaches traffic. Terraform/IaC: add 'upgrade_strategy' block with options: health_first, time_based, manual_canary. Add variables: max_concurrent_replacements, priming_window_seconds, health_gate_thresholds, rollback_policy.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): provision 1 replacement node in a dedicated upgrade group, mirror 5% of production requests using traffic mirroring for 10 minutes, measure error rate, latency, GPU utilization, and memory. Phase 2 (ramp): if canary passes, increase replacements in batches of 2 nodes with 30-minute observation windows. Phase 3 (complete): final sweep replaced with full verification. Safety: dynamic circuit-breaker stops ramp if rolling error-rate > configured multiplier or any tenant sees sustained 5xx. Default cadence: 15-minute priming, 10-minute smoke, 30-minute observation per batch. Operators should support pause/resume and manual continue via Console.
rollback_plan: Rollback is automatic on gate failure: 1) Operator reassigns NLB weights back to previous nodes and marks newly created nodes NotReady; 2) If rollback fails to restore baseline within 10 minutes, alert oncall and create incident. 3) Operator retains logs and metrics for failed upgrade; store snapshot of new node config for analysis. Manual rollback steps added to runbook (Console action: 'Abort Upgrade') with playbook for network/firewall troubleshooting in VPC installs.
test_plan: Unit tests for operator state transitions, end-to-end in staging with a full VPC stack. Generate synthetic workloads: steady-state text-gen at 50 RPS, long-stream sessions to test cache draining, and embedding bursts. Add chaos test: forcibly drop one replacement node mid-drain to validate operator re-attachment and session failover. Add load tests that validate latency percentiles under replacement. Create a post-upgrade validation suite that runs against a canary tenant set.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-node health pane, per-tenant request success rate, KV cache hit ratio, priming success metric, and upgrade operator timeline. Alerts: UpgradeAbort (if health gates fail), RollbackFail (if rollback doesn't converge within timeout), HighTailLatencyDuringUpgrade (>2x baseline), and HighErrorRateDuringUpgrade (>3x baseline). Integrations: Slack channel #infra-upgrades, PagerDuty escalation for production failures. Also emit audit events to customer audit logs in Private installs.
